hook.belief: Nokia died because it was too slow to build a smartphone.
hook.gap: If Nokia had the smartphone first, what actually killed it?

scenes.narration: Nokia never missed the smartphone. It sold one a full decade before the iPhone existed.
scenes.visual_intent: A sales chart where a Nokia line starts a decade before the iPhone marker appears.

facts.claim: Nokia released the 9000 Communicator in 1996; the first iPhone went on sale in 2007.

scenes.narration: So when the iPhone arrived, Nokia owned about half of all smartphone sales.
scenes.visual_intent: A share ring fills to about half in Nokia's colour as the iPhone marker lands.

facts.claim: Nokia held roughly half of worldwide smartphone sales in 2007.

scenes.narration: But hardware never failed. The real threat sat inside Nokia, and its own engineers saw it.
scenes.visual_intent: The chart cracks from the inside; an internal warning card slides out of the Nokia line.

facts.claim: Nokia staff raised concerns about Symbian internally before the iPhone launch.

scenes.narration: Symbian was built for buttons, so touch features took months.
scenes.visual_intent: A keypad grid struggles to redraw as a touch grid while a release timer keeps slipping.

facts.claim: Symbian was designed for keypad phones and adapting it to touch took Nokia a long time.

scenes.narration: But slow code was survivable. Managers feared bad news, therefore every delay stayed hidden from the top.
scenes.visual_intent: Status reports turn from red to green as they climb an org chart toward the top.

facts.claim: A 2015 study by Vuori and Huy found Nokia middle managers withheld bad news out of fear.

scenes.narration: So Nokia kept promising until 2013, when it sold its phones to Microsoft.
scenes.visual_intent: The Nokia share line falls to the floor and a sale stamp lands on it.

facts.claim: Nokia agreed to sell its devices business to Microsoft in 2013.

scenes.narration: No better phone beat Nokia. Its own silence did.
scenes.visual_intent: The falling line loops back into the opening chart with the first caption returning.
